Component styles, states, and other variations all reference other Main components up to a single source Main component.
Architecture diagrams give an overview of how the components are constructed & nested. Most components will have 2-4 layers of nested Main components.

States are always the lowest level of component architecture. Different component states (hover, active, etc) use the Default State component as their Main component. In this example, the Hover, Active, and Disabled states use the Selected Default State component as their Main component.

The top level of the component architecture is the Main Component for all the variations and states. In this example, making changes to the Main Checkbox component will affect all other checkboxes except for where there are overrides.

In Figma, any component that is not an instance is considered a Main component. In this documentation & library all components are Main components. When refering to a component’s “Main component” we are refering to the component that is restyled and recomponentized (its first child in the layers panel). In this example, Checkbox / Selected (Disabled) uses the Main component Checkbox / Selected. In addition, the Main Component in an achitecture diagram (top level) is the single source for all other Main components.

Types and Variations are typically only a single layer between Main components and States (buttons are an example where multiple Types are needed). In this example, Selected, Unselected, and Indeterminate checkbox components use the Main checkbox as their Main component.
Checkbox / Selected (Disabled)’s Main component is Checkbox / Selected
